chunks: And Muhammad ibn Hammam narrated to us, saying: Ja'far ibn Muhammad ibn Malik narrated to me, saying: 'Abbad ibn Ya'qub narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan ibn Hammad al-Ta'i narrated to me, from Abu al-Jarood, from Abu Ja'far Muhammad ibn Ali (peace be upon him), that he said:
The master of this matter is the homeless, fugitive man, who loses his father, who is surnamed with his uncle's name, who is separated from his family, and whose name is the name of a prophet.

key_terms.الشَّرِيدُ: The fugitive or one who flees
key_terms.الطَّرِيدُ: The homeless or one who has been cast out
key_terms.الْمَكْنَّى: The one with a kunya (nominal appellation)
key_terms.الْمَوْتُورُ: The one who loses his father (or is cut off from him)
key_terms.صَاحِبُ الْأَمْرِ: The master of the matter (referring to the Imam)

ai.seo_question: What are the key characteristics of the Mahdi as described in this hadith from Kitab al-Ghayba?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Nu'mani’s *Kitab al-Ghayba* identifies the Twelfth Imam, Muhammad ibn al-Hasan, through specific epithets such as 'al-Tarid' (the exiled) and 'al-Sharid' (the scattered), which historically correlate with his early life and the period of the Minor Occultation. The reference to being 'named after a prophet' confirms his name as Muhammad, aligning with the prophetic tradition of the Mahdi sharing the Prophet's name and attributes, while 'master of the matter' (Sahib al-Amr) denotes his absolute authority in the eschatological era.

en.abdullah-al-shahin: (24) Muhammad bin Hammam narrated from Ja’far bin Muhammad bin Malik from Abbad bin Ya’qoob from al-Hasan bin Hammad at-Ta’iy from Abul Jarood that Abu Ja’far Muhammad bin Ali al-Baqir (as) had said: “
The man of this matter is the homeless, fugitive man, who loses his father, who is surnamed with his uncle’s name, who is separated from his family and whose name is like a prophet’s name.”
